title: openalex_W2133122533
universal_lens: Temporal discretization of aircraft motion under MPC constraints enables structured optimization of trajectory conflicts via parallelized computational kernels. Fuel and CO2 savings across aircraft scenarios; noise pollution cost functions with altitude penalties; population density maps via Gaussian kernels; trajectory optimization under multi-objective constraints.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference maps flight path uncertainty to probabilistic conflict zones using observed telemetry; conformal prediction ensures robustness against adversarial perturbations in airspace dynamics. Bayesian inference on fuel efficiency gains and CO2 reductions using probabilistic models over simulated aircraft trajectories; conformal prediction of environmental impact under varying density scenarios.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning models sequential state transitions through conflict resolution logic gates, enabling real-time decision-making under dynamic airspace constraints. Situational reasoning engine maps aircraft paths through noise-cost augmented space-time fields, transitioning states based on altitude-dependent penalties and population density gradients to optimize flight corridors.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 3 delves into the simulation architecture and empirical validation of a Model Predictive Control (MPC) framework tailored for air traffic management within a Terminal Maneuvering Area (TMA). The core methodology employs a fixed time-step MPC with a horizon of six steps, operating at 10-second intervals, which aligns with modern ATC update cycles but may not fully capture real-world variability. Simulations utilize standardized aircraft dynamics derived from BADA, ensuring consistency while abstracting complex aerodynamic behaviors. The TMA is modeled as a circular region with a central runway, simplifying spatial conflict modeling. Parallel computation is implemented using NVIDIA Tesla C2070 hardware, optimizing performance through thread-block layouts. Results demonstrate that departure and arrival trajectories adapt dynamically to flow fields, indicating effective conflict mitigation strategies. The study emphasizes computational efficiency and scalability, particularly when handling multiple aircraft simultaneously. These findings support the integration of MPC-based algorithms into real-time air traffic systems, offering a foundation for future research in autonomous airspace coordination and adaptive control policies.
